description: "Bitcoin Battlefield" by Nick Greenawalt (motionbynick.com, self-billed "inventor of the Million Dollar Toilet"), hosted on Cloudflare Pages. It is NOT a chart with sprites on it — it's a full 3D Three.js war diorama where the live Binance feed literally IS the battle. Two armies of low-poly plastic toy soldiers (green = buyers, red = sellers) face off across a procedural terrain field; the frontline's position on the field IS the current price (a ±2% band around an anchor maps to field depth, with $-labeled price gridlines lying across the terrain like contour lines). Binance WebSocket streams (depth20@100ms + aggTrade, with host fallback vision→binance.us→binance.com) drive everything: order-book depth sets each army's headcount, every trade kills soldiers on the opposite side, streaks summon air support, and >$220k whale trades trigger cinematic NUKE / GOD CANDLE set-pieces. A procedural market simulator runs until (and whenever) live data isn't flowing, so the screen is never dead. Supports BTC/ETH/SOL, three camera modes (auto-cinematic director, follow, free WASD fly), procedural WebAudio SFX + looping mp3, mobile touch controls, and a live chat over a Cloudflare Worker WebSocket (wss://bitcoin-battlefield-chat.nickgreenawalt.workers.dev/) with nickname join, message history, presence count, and system messages. Whole thing is ONE static HTML file (~1,200 lines) with an importmap pulling three.js from CDN — no build, no backend except the chat Worker.
layout: Full-screen WebGL canvas with a CRT scanline overlay div on top. HUD chrome floats over it: (1) big price + daily % + "BUYERS/SELLERS ARE WINNING TODAY!" headline rendered as a DOM element but screen-space-projected so it hovers in 3D above the frontline; (2) "Killfeed" combat-log panel (6 timestamped rows) bottom-center/left; (3) top-right button stack: BTC/ETH/SOL, Cinematic/Follow/Free, Sim/Live, Speed + Density sliders; (4) bottom-left panel: "Chaos" slider (CALM→MAX), Music/SFX volume sliders, WASD/Q/E/1-2-3 keys legend; (5) "● LIVE" status badge top-left; (6) creator credit top-center; (7) green "● Chat" button bottom-right toggling a 330px chat panel (nickname join row → message input, auto-scroll with stick-to-bottom, ●N online). Mobile collapses panels, makes HUD pointer-events:none so finger drags reach the canvas, and swaps in a Free/Cinematic toggle button.
mechanics: Core mapping engine (all constants in one CONFIG block): (a) BOOK→ARMIES: top 18 bid/ask levels each contribute ceil(8*log10(1+qty/unit)) soldiers (unit=0.05 BTC), summed and capped at 2000/side; on each book update armies reconcile — reinforcements spawn at their own edge and march to formation rows behind the frontline; shrinking depth just stops reinforcing (attrition thins ranks, no retreat). (b) PRICE→FRONTLINE: frontZ = clamp((price−anchor)/(anchor*0.02))·halfField, plus a decaying "flow" impulse (+0.06 per kill toward the winner, exp decay) so kills visibly shove the line; anchor slowly recenters after a >72%-of-band move. (c) TRADE→KILLS: kills = ceil(6*log10(1+notionalUSD/400)), cap 80; buys kill red, sells kill green; attackers fire arcing tracers with random delays, victim death commits when the tracer lands, spawning a ragdoll corpse (gravity, bounce, spin, shrink-out) + a 💀 sprite popping over the body; 10% of deaths get a Wile E. Coyote delayed tip-over. Killfeed line per trade: "🟢 BUY 0.123 — 14 red down". Kills ≥8 add camera shake; gunshot SFX scale with log2(kills). (d) WHALES: notional ≥ $220k → sell = "☢ NUKE" (missile drops on the losing army's rear, boom flash, expanding shock ring, permanent terrain scorch via vertex-color darkening, 0.35x slow-mo, camera hijack-cut to impact) ; buy = "▲ GOD CANDLE" (volumetric green beam from the sky, victims flung straight upward). (e) STREAKS: sampled at 1 Hz — N consecutive same-direction seconds spawn escalating support (jet airstrike → tank → helicopter gunship, each with its own area-kill loop and killfeed emoji); a 16s streak force-triggers a synthetic whale. The Chaos slider (1–8) directly sets the streak threshold (9−v). (f) HONEST SCOREBOARD: in LIVE mode the % and the WINNING headline are measured against the real daily-open kline (fetched, refreshed every 5 min), not an arbitrary anchor. (g) SIM fallback: gaussian drift + momentum regimes + Poisson trades + random order-book "walls" + a forced whale every 55–150s, handing over seamlessly when the first live packet arrives.
aesthetic: Low-poly "plastic army men" 3D, not pixel art: soldiers are ~10 merged primitive parts (helmet, rifle, toy-base disc under the feet — deliberately toy-soldier), flat-shaded, vertex-tinted, drawn as InstancedMesh (2000/side + corpse pools + tracer pools). World is sunny and pastoral on purpose — FBM-noise terrain with a mud strip at the frontline, infinite grass plane, blue gradient sky shader, fog, soft shadows, ACES tonemapping — which makes the carnage funnier. HUD is green-phosphor military-terminal: ui-monospace everywhere, near-black #0a0e0d background, translucent blurred panels, thin desaturated-green borders, scanline overlay; palette green #5fd06a / red #ff5a52 / amber #ffc24b. Team colors: toy-green army vs toy-red army with lime/orange tracers. Tone is deadpan absurdist comedy: "GOD CANDLE", "buyers vaporized", "sellers routed", 💀 emoji death marks, Wile E. Coyote falls, "Chaos: INSANE", killfeed like an FPS, klaxon + falling-bomb whistle synthesized in WebAudio. Zero art assets except one music.mp3 — every texture (muzzle flash, skull, labels) is a runtime canvas.
ideas_to_steal: Frontline-as-metric: the battle line's position IS the number (price in a ±2% band) plus a decaying per-kill 'flow' shove — map ours to spam's share of current block weight / mempool vbytes, so filters visibly hold or lose ground.

SIM-until-live handover: a procedural generator (drift + momentum + Poisson events + forced set-pieces) drives the scene instantly and during any disconnect, and live data takes over on first packet — do the same with a fake mempool until mempool.space WS connects, with endpoint-rotation fallback and a ● LIVE badge.
Log-scale everything: soldiers = 8·log10(1+qty/unit), kills = 6·log10(1+notional/$400) with caps — whale inscriptions stay legible instead of nuking the scene, dust spam still registers as one goon.

Streak-escalation tiers + a user-facing 'Chaos' slider that literally edits the threshold constant (CALM→INSANE): consecutive spam-heavy blocks summon escalating set-pieces (jet→tank→gunship for them; ours: Ordinals Airship → Rune Etcher Tank → 'datacarrier=0 Patch Drop' gunship).

Whale set-pieces with camera hijack, slow-mo, and PERMANENT terrain scorch (vertex colors darkened forever): a 4MB wizard-JPEG inscription = '🖼 JPEG NUKE', a mass filter-node deployment = green 'FILTER BEAM' god candle; scorch marks become a visible history of the session's biggest events.

FPS-style Killfeed as the comedy engine: timestamped emoji one-liners for every event ('🟢 BUY 0.123 — 14 red down', '☢ NUKE $410k — buyers vaporized') — ours writes itself: '🖼 leather-jacket JPEG breaches block 903,441 — 12 filtrators down', '🛡 mempoolfullrbf holds the line'.
Cheap physical comedy that lands: ragdoll corpses with bounce + spin, 💀 sprite popping over each body, and a 10% 'Wile E. Coyote' delayed tip-over — plus screen shake and 0.35x slow-mo on big events.

Honest scoreboard trick: the 'BUYERS ARE WINNING TODAY!' headline is measured against the real daily-open kline (refetched every 5 min), not internal state — ours should headline a real verifiable stat (e.g. % of today's block space that is inscriptions) so the satire has teeth.

Auto-cinematic camera director (random 7–10s dolly/orbit/push-in/overview shots, event-triggered cuts, then resume) makes it an ambient leave-on-a-monitor / stream-overlay toy — plus Free WASD fly mode for poking around.

The whole delivery model: ONE static HTML file (importmap + CDN three.js, InstancedMesh pools, runtime-canvas textures, procedural WebAudio SFX — zero assets, zero build) on Cloudflare Pages, with the only backend a ~100-line Cloudflare Worker WebSocket chat (join/msg/history/presence/system, nick in localStorage) — a 'Trench Chat' clone is an afternoon of work.
